directSourceFindings: workflow-stage13-closure.js derives the current run identities from the frozen iteration and rejects any current comparison state that does not resolve to exactly ten runs.

The Stage 13 closure derives the canonical required verification relation set and requires exactly one current verification for every due REQ_ID × RUN_ID × TEST_ID tuple; missing and duplicate tuples fail closed.
Each required test contributes its frozen EXPECTED_VARIANCE_CONTRACT and the comparison model binds the resulting contract hash set to the derived requirement facts.

Aggregate comparison truth is application-owned: ALL_TEN_SATISFIED, ANY_VIOLATION, ANY_UNDETERMINED, satisfaction counts, verification IDs, evidence IDs, and expected-variance-contract hashes are derived from canonical current verification records.
UNKNOWN variance authorization is blocked, and application-derived UNDETERMINED truth is blocked rather than silently reduced to a favorable state.
Correctness-affecting or prohibited output variance requires an explicit DEFECT_IDS handoff to Stage 14 before Stage 13 can close that comparison record.
A current VIOLATED verification tuple is retained as ANY_VIOLATION=true and routed forward; the closure explicitly rejects the legacy behavior that blocked every verified violation at Stage 13.
Comparison evidence is derived across all required current verification records and preserved evidence references; no current run or required verification evidence is discarded.
verify-cross-run-comparison.mjs is wired into verify-spec-residual-closure.mjs, so the positive, negative, and repaired comparison fixtures execute in the permanent definition-of-done chain.

The repaired Stage 17 fixture includes the accepted independent applicability semantic review required by the current Stage 05 authority semantics, so Stage 13 proof does not bypass or weaken earlier applicability gates.
